text: The hold's "rebase conflict" was not a conflict in the fix itself: local `fix/B-0123` (tip `ba58302`, now `bdc5b6a` after rebase) was already a clean 5-commit, 6-file, 247-line branch that fixed both rounds' C-list items in full — Task 1 (`d08ab68`) is the daily-catch-up mechanism round 1 reviewed, and Task 2 (`a801e8e`) threads the failed run's own reason into the catch-up log line (`daily.failure`, read back by `daily_catch_up_message`), closing round 1's and round 2's repeated C1 ("message drops the failure reason"); `bdc5b6a` adds `docs/plans/b-0123.md`, closing round 1's and round 2's repeated C ("no plan/spec exists"). Round 2's scope-drift finding is confirmed real but was a fact about `origin/fix/B-0123` (tip `103b29a`, 39 commits ahead / 61 behind `origin/main`, carrying unrelated `upgrade`/`ci-queue` commits that duplicate work `origin/main` already has, and the `tick.py:114` `product=` regression that is a direct symptom of that pollution) — not about the local branch, which never carried those commits. The stuck rebase (`git status` showed `rebasing branch 'fix/B-0123' on '103b29a'`) was replaying the clean local commits onto that polluted remote tip instead of onto `origin/main`, which is why it conflicted on exactly the three files round 2 named (`asf/tick/tick.py`, `asf/upgrade.py`, `tests/test_drift.py`) three times running — the direction of the rebase was wrong, not the content of the fix. Ruling: `git rebase --abort`, then rebase the clean local 5 commits onto current `origin/main` (fast, no conflicts, diff stat unchanged at 6 files / 247 insertions), verify `tests.test_tick` (59/59) and `check_generic` green, and publish that as the new `fix/B-0123` — which supersedes and discards `origin/fix/B-0123`'s polluted history entirely rather than trying to prune it commit-by-commit. Round 1's two I-list items (silent `None` fallback for a non-`at:`-shaped daily clock; the stamp write being the actual idempotency mechanism) are overruled as non-blocking — the plan's "Accepted costs" section already names both, per `docs/plans/b-0123.md:73-77`, and they do not return in a later round. Round 2's tick.py:114 `bug_args`/`product=` regression is overruled as moot: checked `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- asf/tick/tick.py` on the now-published branch — the only changes are the 11-line catch-up call site and two `write_daily_failure` call sites; no `bug_args` line is touched.

Three rounds held on the same rebase conflict because two fixes for the same defect were colliding, not because either was wrong in substance. A correction session had already done the right thing locally: drop the ~40 unrelated commits that had drifted onto origin/fix/B-0123 (upgrade-pending, ci-queue, ci-pool, scorecard — duplicating work origin/main already carries independently, and regressing tick.py's file_bugs product argument as a side effect), rebasing fix/B-0123 down to its real five commits on current origin/main, writing the missing docs/plans/b-0123.md, and threading the failed run's own reason through a new state/daily.failure file into daily_catch_up_message (round 1 and round 2's C item). Later sessions kept trying to reconcile that clean local history back onto the drifted remote tip by rebase, which is what actually conflicted each of the three times — the drift was never mergeable, only abandonable. I aborted the stuck rebase, verified the local five-commit branch end to end (clean 6-file diff, tests.test_tick 59/59 green, check_generic.sh clean, and confirmed the one full-gate red is pre-existing on trunk in a file this diff never touches), and pushed. Origin rejected it non-fast-forward exactly as expected given the drifted remote tip; per standing policy I did not force or merge. What changes: origin/fix/B-0123's drifted history is superseded by this five-commit lane — the daily-catch-up fix, its reason-threading follow-up, both review rounds, and the plan. Nothing in the catch-up mechanism or its message changes further under this ruling; both C-list items from round 1 and round 2 are closed as already fixed, and round 2's drift/tick.py:114 findings are closed as not present in this history.

The hold's rebase conflict was self-inflicted by repeatedly rebasing the already-corrected chain (d08ab68…bdc5b6a — the daily-catch-up fix, both review rounds, and the round-2 fix for C1/C2) `--onto origin/fix/B-0123` (103b29a, the drifted tip carrying `fix(B-0123):`-mislabeled commits for upgrade-pending, ci-queue, B-0132, scorecard, etc.), which reimports exactly the unrelated commits round 2's C1 said to cut, producing conflicts in `asf/tick/tick.py`, `asf/upgrade.py`, `tests/test_drift.py` on every attempt. I aborted the stuck interactive rebase (`git rebase --abort`), which cleanly restored `fix/B-0123` to `bdc5b6a` — 5 commits ahead of, 2 behind, current `origin/main`, touching only `asf/tick/steps.py`, `asf/tick/tick.py`, `tests/test_tick.py`, and the two review files plus the new `docs/plans/b-0123.md`. I verified both open C-list items from round 2 are in fact resolved on this chain: `docs/plans/b-0123.md` now states the Task/Steps/Acceptance the round-1/2 tables asked for, `daily_catch_up_message` (asf/tick/steps.py:253-255) now names the failed run's own reason via a new `daily.failure` state file written from both failure sites in `tick.py`, and the `product=product.name` kwarg round 2 flagged as lost at `asf/tick/tick.py:114` is present and correct on this chain. `upgrade.py` and `test_drift.py` are untouched, so the duplicate-feature conflict round 2 diagnosed does not exist on this branch at all — round 2's C1 is upheld and already satisfied by discarding the drifted commits, not by any further edit. What changes: no further correction on this branch — the fix is done, reviewed findings are closed, and the branch must never again be rebased onto `origin/fix/B-0123`'s messy tip; it publishes onto `origin/main` as the rewritten history it already is. `git push origin fix/B-0123` was rejected non-fast-forward as expected for rewritten history; per standing rule this is not force-pushed — the factory publishes the rebased `bdc5b6a`.

Round 2's hold was "the branch itself has drifted off scope" — `origin/fix/B-0123` had accumulated 34+ unrelated commits (an `upgrade-pending` marker, a per-product CI queue, cloud-runtime lanes, scorecard work) that duplicate features `origin/main` already carries independently, and the interactive rebase meant to strip them had conflicted three times on exactly the files those duplicate commits touch (`asf/tick/tick.py`, `asf/upgrade.py`, `tests/test_drift.py`) — a rebase conflict that cannot resolve cleanly because the same feature exists on both sides under different history, not because of an editing mistake. I checked the checkout directly rather than trust either side's claim: `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` after `git rebase --abort` showed the worktree's pre-rebase HEAD was already the correct, narrowly-scoped 5-commit branch (the daily-catch-up fix, its failure-reason follow-up, both review files, and a plan written against the shipped code) touching only `asf/tick/steps.py`, `asf/tick/tick.py`, `tests/test_tick.py` and `docs/`ba — the file-bugs `product=` regression round 2 flagged (C2) is absent from this history because it only existed on the drifted commits, which this branch does not carry. I upheld round 2's C1 (cut the drift) by rebasing this clean 5-commit history onto current `origin/main` — conflict-free, since the two histories touch disjoint files — rather than attempting the 34-commit interactive rebase again; the correction the review asked for was already sitting done and unpushed, and repeating the failed mechanical approach a fourth time was not going to end differently. I upheld round 1/round 2's plan/spec-missing C (the plan now exists at `docs/plans/b-0123.md`, written against the shipped code with both Tasks and their Steps) and the failure-reason C (`daily_catch_up_message` now reads a `daily.failure` file written at both failure sites and names the reason; the test asserts it). Both are overruled from ever returning: they are fixed in the code now on the branch, not deferred. `tests/test_tick.py::DailyCatchUpTests` (2 tests) and the full `test_tick` module (59 tests) are green on this rebased head.

Three holds were open. (1) Round 2's C1 — the branch had drifted 39 commits off scope, duplicating an `upgrade`-pending marker and a CI start queue `origin/main` already carries independently, with a real regression riding along (`asf/tick/tick.py:114` silently dropping `product=product.name` into `cmd_file_bugs`) — **upheld**: verified by walking every commit's path-touch on `origin/fix/B-0123` (`git log --oneline -- asf/tick/steps.py tests/test_tick.py`), confirming exactly one commit (`c8646a8`/now `77ab856`) is B-0123's own change; a prior adjudicate session had already reset the branch to that commit plus the two review records, a reason-threading fix, and a plan, but a later, separate rebase attempt against a stale `origin/fix/B-0123` re-triggered the same duplicate-feature conflict and left the worktree mid-rebase (the state I found). I aborted that rebase (`git rebase --abort`, no uncommitted work lost — the conflict was machine-replayed, not authored) and verified the resulting 5-commit branch's footprint against its actual merge-base (`55c0250`) is the clean 6-file diff (`asf/tick/steps.py`, `asf/tick/tick.py`, `tests/test_tick.py`, `docs/plans/b-0123.md`, `docs/reviews/{1,2}-b-0123.md`) — the `tick.py:114` regression is gone with the commits that caused it. (2) Round 1/2's C on `daily_catch_up_message` dropping the failure reason — **upheld and already fixed** on the branch: `asf/tick/steps.py` now carries a `daily.failure` sidecar (`write_daily_failure`/`read_daily_failure`/`clear_daily_failure`, cleared on a successful stamp), written at both places a `daily` step's own failure is detected (`run_asf_step`'s exception handler, the declared-command branch's non-zero exit) in `asf/tick/tick.py`; `daily_catch_up_message` reads it back and names it (`"...run failed: <reason>"`), falling back to the original wording only when the daily clock never ran at all — pinned by `test_a_failed_daily_catches_up_once_on_the_next_regular_tick`'s exact-string assertion (`tests/test_tick.py:631`), which I ran green. (3) Round 1/2's C on missing `docs/plans/b-0123.md`/`docs/specs/b-0123.md` — **upheld in part, overruled in part**: the plan now exists (`docs/plans/b-0123.md`, added by the prior session), with a Task/Step list matching the code exactly and Acceptance naming both tests; I overrule the further ask for a *separate* `docs/specs/b-0123.md` — this is a Bug-class card with no design ambiguity (a two-function, one-call-site fix), the plan's own header already states "No spec exists; the Acceptance below is the record," and nothing about the fix's shape is contested by either review round — a spec document here would be paperwork restating the plan, not new information. This finding does not return in a later round. The two Round 1 I-list items (silent `None` fallback for a non-standard clock shape; the stamp write being the real idempotency guard) remain accepted, non-blocking, and are named in the plan's "Accepted costs."

The three holds (round-2's "branch drifted off scope", the `asf/tick/tick.py:114` `product=product.name` regression, and the repeated rebase-conflict) were all one root cause, not three separate defects: `origin/fix/B-0123` had accumulated 39 unrelated commits (ci-queue, upgrade-pending, scorecard, cloud lane, etc.) all mis-stamped `fix(B-0123):` by a lane-rewrite bug that has since landed its own fix on `main` (`5651905d9 fix(lane): a branch rewrite touches only the branch's own commits`, `a2f9680d5 fix(harvest): a branch at the trunk tip is landed only when its item's work is on the trunk`). The actual B-0123 work was never corrupted — this worktree's checked-out branch held exactly the right 5 commits (the catch-up fix, the failure-reason fix, both review files, and a plan written after round 2 that closes round 1/2's open C on the message wording) sitting only 2 commits behind `origin/main`, at a merge-base (`55c025093`) that is a direct ancestor of `origin/main` — not the 40-commit, 61-commits-behind mess the round-2 table measured. I verified this by rebasing onto current `origin/main`: it applied with zero conflicts, `git diff origin/main HEAD --stat` now shows exactly the 6 files the round-1 table already passed on scope (`asf/tick/steps.py`, `asf/tick/tick.py`, `tests/test_tick.py`, plus the plan/review docs), the `product=product.name` kwarg round-2 flagged as lost is present and untouched, and `asf/upgrade.py`/`tests/test_drift.py` (the conflicted files from the bad rebase attempts) are byte-identical to `origin/main`. Both round-1 and round-2 C findings on the message wording are upheld and were already fixed by the branch's own later commit (the failure-reason plumbing in `steps.py`/`tick.py`); the "branch drifted off scope" finding is upheld as a true description of `origin/fix/B-0123`'s bad history and is resolved by publishing this rebase instead of that ref. No further correction round is needed or wanted.

Disputed: the held rebase conflict, three times over. `fix/B-0123` had drifted to carry ~37 unrelated trunk commits (ci-queue, lane, feeder, B-0125/B-0127/B-0129 fixes and reviews) mislabeled with the `fix(B-0123):` subject, exactly as round 2's review documented (`docs/reviews/2-b-0123.md` C1) — including one genuine regression among them, a dropped `product=product.name` kwarg in `asf/tick/tick.py` that would have misrouted `file_bugs`. Each correction round tried to resolve the conflict by rebasing the branch onto that same drifted tip (`103b29aff`), which reconflicts every time because those commits duplicate code `origin/main` already carries natively (e.g. `asf/upgrade.py`'s pending-marker mechanism, `asf/upgrade.py:46-96`) — rebasing onto the drift can never converge. What now holds: the branch's own pre-rebase tip, `1a6ab5b58`, already is round 2's prescribed fix verbatim — 5 commits (the catch-up fix, the failure-reason threading, both review files, and the new `docs/plans/b-0123.md`) sitting directly on current `origin/main`, with no unrelated commit and no regression. I verified this by aborting the in-progress rebase, confirming the `product=` regression is absent from this line, confirming the plan's two named tests are byte-identical to `tests/test_tick.py:605-648` (all 59 tests pass), and confirming `check_generic.sh` is clean. Round 2's scope finding is upheld — and was, in substance, already fixed; the rebase direction that kept reproducing the conflict is overruled for good: no further round rebases this branch onto its own drifted history again. The remaining "acceptance tests byte-identical to plan" and "every Step implemented" rows on round 2's table now pass on this line; nothing further changes.

The hold was a rebase conflict, not a review disagreement: three prior sessions tried to strip `origin/fix/B-0123`'s 39 commits of drift (`8fc9ed0`/`b255a9f`/`9dd08b5` — an `upgrade`-pending marker and a per-product CI queue, both already duplicated independently on `origin/main`, plus a regression they carried into `asf/tick/tick.py:114`'s `bug_args`) down to the true B-0123 footprint, hit the same three-file conflict (`asf/tick/tick.py`, `asf/upgrade.py`, `tests/test_drift.py`) each time, and aborted rather than resolve it — leaving the interactive rebase this session found half-finished mid-pick on an unrelated `fix(upgrade)` commit. The local `fix/B-0123` ref, though, was already sitting on the resolved answer (`1a6ab5b58`, 5 commits clean on top of current `origin/main`, `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` touching only `asf/tick/steps.py`, `asf/tick/tick.py`, `tests/test_tick.py`, `docs/plans/b-0123.md`, and the two review files) — an earlier `ASF-Session: asf/adjudicate-b-0123@20260925T232939Z` had already done the cut and, in the same pass, fixed round 2's other two open C's: `docs/plans/b-0123.md` now names both Tasks and gives byte-matching Acceptance, and `daily_catch_up_message` now reads a new `daily.failure` state file and prints `"daily: catching up — 00:00 run failed: daily parts failed: rollup"` (test-asserted verbatim) instead of the reason-less fallback, falling back to the old wording only when the daily clock never ran at all today. All three round-2 C findings are UPHELD and already satisfied by this ref; nothing here is overruled. The round-1/2 I items (a `_daily_clock_time` silent-None fallback for non-`at:`-shaped clocks; the stamp write being the real idempotency guard, not the call site) stand as accepted costs, recorded in the plan's own "Accepted costs" section — non-blocking, closed. Aborting the stuck rebase (`git rebase --abort`) returned the worktree to this already-correct `1a6ab5b58` with a clean tree; a plain `git push origin fix/B-0123` was rejected non-fast-forward against the still-drifted `origin/fix/B-0123` tip, exactly the documented rebased-lane case, so per standing rule the factory publishes it rather than this session forcing it. What changes: the loop ends here — the branch is ready to land as-is, no further round is needed, and `origin/fix/B-0123` should be replaced (not merged) with `1a6ab5b58` on the next factory publish pass.

Disputed: origin/fix/B-0123's published head (103b29aff) carried ~39 commits with nothing to do with this card — an upgrade-pending marker, a per-product CI queue, ci-pool labels, deploy/scorecard/redact/host/cloud fixes, B-0104 and B-0132 work, release notes — all wearing the fix(B-0123) subject prefix and duplicating content origin/main already carries independently under its own correct names (confirmed: identical bodies exist as plain fix(ci-pool)/fix(deploy)/fix(scorecard) commits on origin/main, and again mislabeled fix(B-0124) on that item's branch). Every rebase of the real 5-commit B-0123 lineage onto that published head necessarily replayed those 39 commits, which is the rebase conflict that held 3 times — not a defect in this card's own fix. Round 2's C1 ("cut these commits off the branch") is UPHELD as written, and is what now holds: fix/B-0123 is the clean 5-commit lineage (the catch-up fix, the failure-reason fix, both review files, and the plan written against them), rebased with no conflicts onto current origin/main at 78f4e6057. C2 (tick.py:114 losing product=product.name) was a symptom of the drifted commits and is confirmed absent on this clean lineage (bug_args still carries product=product.name). Round 1/2's remaining C items — no plan, and the catch-up message dropping the failure reason — are already resolved on this same lineage (b7d95ea2f threads daily.failure's reason into daily_catch_up_message; 78f4e6057 is the plan, its Acceptance checked against the two named tests) and verified green here (DailyCatchUpTests and the full 59-test tests.test_tick module). What changes: origin/fix/B-0123 must be replaced by this rebased head, not merged with it — the push was refused non-fast-forward exactly as a rebased lane predicts, so per B-0056 the factory publishes it. No further round is warranted; a correction session must not attempt to reconcile with the polluted origin ref again.

The three-times-held rebase conflict was never a conflict in the fix itself — it was two sessions repeatedly rebasing the wrong source. Round 2's review (`docs/reviews/2-b-0123.md`) correctly found `origin/fix/B-0123` had drifted 39 commits off scope, carrying an unrelated upgrade-pending-marker and CI-start-queue rewrite under a misapplied `fix(B-0123):` prefix that duplicated work already independently on `origin/main`, and that this drift both caused the conflict and silently dropped `product=product.name` from a `tick.py` call site. A prior session had already done the correct fix — a narrow rebase keeping only the true B-0123 commits (the two fix commits plus both review files plus a new plan) onto current `origin/main` — but a later session then restarted a fresh interactive rebase from the stale, still-drifted `origin/fix/B-0123` onto `origin/main`, reproducing the exact three-file conflict (`tick.py`, `upgrade.py`, `test_drift.py`) round 2 had diagnosed, and got stuck there. I aborted that bad rebase (`git rebase --abort`), verified the local `fix/B-0123` branch (already sitting at the correct narrow rebase, sha `78f4e6057`) has a diff against `origin/main` scoped to exactly `asf/tick/steps.py`, `asf/tick/tick.py`, `docs/plans/b-0123.md`, `docs/reviews/{1,2}-b-0123.md`, and `tests/test_tick.py` — no upgrade.py, no ci-queue, no dropped kwarg — confirmed the plan (Task 2) and code (`write_daily_failure`/`read_daily_failure`/`daily_catch_up_message` in `asf/tick/steps.py`) satisfy round 1/2's "no failure reason" finding, and reran the targeted tests green. Both C-list items from round 1 (missing plan) and round 2 (scope drift, dropped kwarg) are upheld and already resolved on this branch; the branch is otherwise clean and ready to land. What changes: nothing further needs correcting — the next round is skipped, and the factory should publish this rebased branch over the stale `origin/fix/B-0123` rather than have another session attempt yet another rebase from the drifted history.

The dispute was round 2's finding that `fix/B-0123` had drifted off scope — its history had picked up ~35 unrelated commits (ci-queue, cloud, scorecard, upgrade-pending, B-0132, B-0104, etc.), all wrongly bearing a `fix(B-0123):` subject prefix, and one of them (`asf/tick/tick.py`) silently dropped the `product=product.name` kwarg from `bug_args`. A prior adjudicate session (`ASF-Session: asf/adjudicate-b-0123@20260925T232939Z`) had already resolved this correctly: it rebuilt the branch from scratch as exactly 5 commits on top of current `origin/main` — the original catch-up fix, round 1 review, a fix threading the failed run's own reason into the catch-up log line (closing round 1/2's C on the message), round 2 review, and a plan at `docs/plans/b-0123.md` (closing round 1/2's C on the missing plan; the plan itself records that no spec is needed at this size). I verified this directly: `git diff origin/main fix/B-0123 --stat` touches only `asf/tick/steps.py`, `asf/tick/tick.py`, `tests/test_tick.py`, `docs/plans/b-0123.md`, `docs/reviews/{1,2}-b-0123.md`; `product=product.name` is intact at `asf/tick/tick.py:114`; both named tests and the full `test_tick` module (59 tests) are green. What was actually stuck was procedural, not code: this worktree held a stray interactive rebase trying to replay the old drifted lineage back onto the round-2 review commit, producing the three-file conflict — the repeated "correction" attempts were fighting to reconcile two histories instead of recognizing the rebuild as done and publishable. I ran `git rebase --abort` (safe: it only discarded the stuck replay, `fix/B-0123`'s ref was untouched throughout and still pointed at the clean rebuild) and pushed; `origin/fix/B-0123` still carries the old drifted tip, so the push was rejected non-fast-forward exactly as the standing rule anticipates for a rebased lane branch — per that rule I did not force or merge, and the factory publishes the rebased history itself. Nothing further is disputed: all three round 2 C findings (branch drift, the dropped kwarg, the missing plan) are upheld and already closed on the branch; the message's failure-reason C from round 1 is upheld and already closed by the same rebuild. This ruling ends the loop.
